## ec5fd031b9e1

**Issue: accepted scenes can have multiple equally short valid paths, so the output depends on undocumented BFS neighbor order rather than the stated rule alone.**

Reproducer: `seed=0`, `sample_index=0`, `difficulty=easy`; `self_check` returns no errors.

```text
8888888888
8000000008
8000000008
8888889888
8000000008
8000000008
8000000008
8900000008
8888888888
```

The color-9 endpoints are `(3,6)` and `(7,1)`. The implementation-selected shortest path has 9 edges:

`(3,6) -> (4,6) -> (5,6) -> (6,6) -> (7,6) -> (7,5) -> (7,4) -> (7,3) -> (7,2) -> (7,1)`

An equally short alternative is:

`(3,6) -> (4,6) -> (5,6) -> (6,6) -> (6,5) -> (7,5) -> (7,4) -> (7,3) -> (7,2) -> (7,1)`

The reproducer enumerated at least 8 shortest paths. Unless the task explicitly teaches a tie-break order, more than one output fits “draw a shortest path.” The generator should either enforce unique shortest paths or make the tie-break observable and part of the rule. Evidence: `checks/audit/ec5fd031b9e1_equal_shortest_paths.json`.
